sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 13

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 13:1
items.html:
Explains the clothing of the Partzufim one within the other, and more, and it contains three matters: A. The necessity that the five Partzufim come out one below the other. B. That the Tabur of the upper one becomes the Peh of the Rosh of the Partzuf below it. And it is found that every Partzuf comes out from the Malchut of Malchut of the upper one, which is called Tabur. C. The order of the clothing of the Partzufim one within the other.

The difference between the five levels one below the other, and the five levels one above the other
Now understand well the difference between the ten Sefirot Keter, Hochma, Bina, ZA, Malchut, which stand one above the other, and the five Partzufim Galgalta, AB, SAG, MA, BON, which stand one below the other. For the ten Sefirot Keter, Hochma, Bina, ZA, and Malchut came out and were emanated at the time of the ascent of the Malchut to the Emanator, which occurs in each and every Partzuf of the five Partzufim (as above, Chapter 10, item 5), since for the birth of a Partzuf, the screen and the Malchut of the preceding Partzuf must rise to the Peh of the Rosh that is there, in order to receive new coarseness in a new form, at which time a new coupling is made for the new Partzuf. This is unlike the ten Sefirot Keter, Hochma, Bina, ZON, which come out at the time of the refinement of the Malchut (as above, Chapter 6, item 5), which do not receive new coarseness, but on the contrary, rise and become refined each time more, and refinement means ascent, and so phase three is emanated above phase four, and phase two above phase three, and so on.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 13:2
items.html:
The Peh of the Rosh of the lower one must come out in the place of the Chazeh of the upper one
This is not so with the emanation of the Partzufim. For example, when Partzuf AB comes out from Partzuf Galgalta, the Malchut of the Guf of Galgalta must rise to the place of the Peh of the Rosh in Galgalta, where she receives coarseness of phase three anew (as above, Chapter 10, items 8-9), the acquiring of the coarseness meaning that she returns to her place, to the Tabur of Partzuf Galgalta as at first, as written there, that the new coupling by striking in phase three is made necessarily in the place of the Tabur (now called Chazeh, as we shall see) of Partzuf Galgalta. You thus see, that the Malchut of the Rosh of Partzuf AB is in the place of the Tabur of Partzuf Galgalta, from which it always follows, that the Malchut of the Guf of the upper Partzuf becomes the Malchut of the Rosh for the Partzuf below it, meaning that the Tabur of the upper one becomes the Peh of the Rosh of the lower one.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 13:3
items.html:
The five Partzufim must come out one below the other
In such a way, that the mouth of the Tabur of Galgalta becomes the Peh of the Rosh of AB, and the mouth of the Tabur of AB becomes the Peh of the Rosh of SAG, and the mouth of the Tabur of SAG becomes the Peh of the Rosh of MA. And the mouth of the Tabur of MA becomes the Peh of the Rosh of BON. Thus, the five Partzufim must come out one below the other, contrary to the individual ten Sefirot in each and every Partzuf, which come out one above the other.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 13:4
items.html:
Every Partzuf comes out from the Malchut of Malchut of the upper one
And from here we derive the rule, that every Partzuf is emanated by force of the Malchut of Malchut that is in the upper one. For it has been explained, that the Malchut of the Guf that is in the upper Partzuf, called the Tabur of the upper one, is the Emanator of the second Partzuf to it, since, for example, through the ascent of the Tabur of Partzuf Galgalta to the Peh of the Rosh of Galgalta, it is found that it receives there coarseness of phase three, upon whose coupling the second Partzuf, called AB, as above, is emanated and comes out. And behold, this Tabur of Galgalta is the Malchut of Malchut of Galgalta, since the Peh is Malchut and the Tabur is the Malchut of Malchut, as above, hence, the Malchut of Malchut of the upper one is the root and the Emanator of the one below it.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 13:5
items.html:
The order of the clothing of the five Partzufim of AK upon one another
And with this you will also understand the order of the clothing among the five Partzufim of AK. For the Peh of the Rosh of Partzuf AB stands in the place of the Tabur of Partzuf Galgalta, as above (item 3), and extends from below upward, up to the Peh of the Rosh of Galgalta, since there it is regarded as the end of the level of the ten Sefirot of the Rosh of AB, because of the Tabur of Galgalta that rose there, and received the coarseness for the sake of its coupling, as above (item 2), and therefore we say that the ten Sefirot of the Rosh of AB stand and clothe the ten Sefirot of the Toch of Galgalta, meaning from the Peh to the Tabur, as explained. In such a way, that the Rosh of Partzuf Galgalta remains uncovered, without clothing.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 13:6
items.html:
The reason there is no clothing in the Rosh
And in the same way too, the ten Sefirot of the Rosh of Partzuf SAG clothe the ten Sefirot of the Toch of Galgalta. And likewise the ten Sefirot of the Rosh of Partzuf MA clothe the ten Sefirot of the Toch of Partzuf SAG, and so on, likewise for the same reason mentioned above regarding the clothing of AB upon Partzuf Galgalta, since one reason applies to all of them, for they all come out by the force of the ascent of the Tabur of the upper one to the Peh of the upper one, and therefore the place where the ten Sefirot of the Rosh of the lower one stand is in the place of the ten Sefirot of the Toch of the upper one, meaning from the Peh to the Tabur. And from the Peh upward of every upper one, it always remains uncovered, without any clothing whatsoever.
